title: Too tired to brush
scene: It's late, you're already in bed, and your teeth feel fine.

options.text: Skip brushing, just this once.
Get up and brush for two minutes.

outcomes.setback: Your gums feel sore at breakfast.
outcomes.disaster: A toothache, then a filling at the dentist, and a 50-coin bill.
outcomes.good: The dentist says your teeth are looking great.
outcomes.lucky: No fillings again. The dentist gives you a sticker and a new toothbrush.
outcomes.why: Two minutes a night adds up to strong teeth for life.

title: One more video
scene: It's devices-off time, and the next video has already started playing.

options.text: Watch just one more, then another.
Turn it off and read in bed.

outcomes.setback: You yawn all the way through maths.
outcomes.disaster: You're so tired you trip in the playground and sprain your wrist.
outcomes.good: You wake up before your alarm, full of energy.
outcomes.lucky: Best sleep ever. You win your race at sport.
outcomes.why: Screens off early means better sleep, and sleep powers everything else.

title: Rainy training
scene: It's drizzling and tennis starts in 20 minutes. The couch looks very comfy.

options.text: Stay home and play video games.
Grab a jacket and go.

outcomes.setback: Your serve is rusty at the next match.
outcomes.disaster: You miss so much training that you're dropped from the team.
outcomes.good: Only three kids turn up, so you get extra coaching.
outcomes.lucky: The coach notices your effort and makes you captain for the day.
outcomes.why: Showing up when it's hard is how you get good.

title: Swim between the flags
scene: At the beach, your friends want to swim near the rocks, where there are no lifeguards.

options.text: Go with your friends to the rocks.
Swim between the red and yellow flags.

outcomes.setback: A wave knocks you over and you scrape your knee.
outcomes.disaster: The water pulls you away from the shore. A lifeguard paddles out on a board to bring you back. You're safe, but very shaken.
outcomes.good: The lifeguards run a bodyboard race, and you're right there to join in.
outcomes.lucky: You catch the best wave of the day all the way to the sand.
outcomes.why: The flags mark the safest water. Smart swimmers always use them.

title: Carnival day
scene: It's a hot, sunny athletics carnival. Your hat is in your bag, and none of your friends are wearing one.

options.text: Leave the hat in your bag so you fit in.
Hat on, sunscreen on.

outcomes.setback: A sunburnt nose and shoulders. Ouch.
outcomes.disaster: Bad sunburn and too much heat. You spend the afternoon in sick bay and miss your races.
outcomes.good: You stay cool and run a personal best.
outcomes.lucky: You win a ribbon in the long jump.
outcomes.why: Slip, slop, slap. Looking after your skin today looks after it for life.

title: Just around the corner
scene: Your friend lives just around the corner. Your bike helmet is in the garage, and it squashes your hair.

options.text: Ride without it. It's not far.
Helmet on, every ride.

outcomes.setback: You wobble off the kerb and graze your elbow.
outcomes.disaster: You hit a pothole, fall and bump your head. Mum takes you to hospital to get checked.
outcomes.good: You and your friend ride to the park and back with no dramas.
outcomes.lucky: A police officer at the park gives you a free ice-cream voucher for riding safely.
outcomes.why: A helmet only works if it's on your head.

title: Snack attack
scene: You're starving after school. There are chips and soft drink in the cupboard, and fruit and yoghurt in the fridge.

options.text: Chips and soft drink.
A handful of chips with an apple.
Fruit, yoghurt and a glass of water.

outcomes.setback: An hour later you feel tired and cranky.
outcomes.disaster: A tummy ache and no energy. You lose your tennis match 6-0.
outcomes.good: Full of energy, you finish a whole building set in one go.
outcomes.lucky: You feel great and beat your own record around the block.
outcomes.why: Food is fuel. Better fuel, better day.

title: Rep team trials
scene: Trials for the district tennis team are on Saturday. Only fit, well-practised players get picked.

options.text: Skip trials this year.
Go to the trials.

outcomes.normal: Close, but not picked. The coach says to come back next season.
outcomes.good: Picked as a reserve. Rep team cards unlock.
outcomes.lucky: Picked for the team, and your character gets the team shirt.
outcomes.why: Big chances go to people who've been getting ready all along.

title: A new dojo
scene: Mum and Dad found a martial arts class near home. It's two sessions a week, starting as a white belt.

options.text: Not now. Stay home and play video games.
Sign up and commit to the term.

later.text: a 150 XP Seed after your first four classes, the Martial arts habit unlocks

outcomes.good: The instructor says you're a natural.
outcomes.lucky: You're picked to help show the class a new move.
outcomes.ifA: No risk token. The card comes back next week with a 30 XP bonus, and Mum and Dad get a note.
outcomes.why: Every black belt was once a white belt who said yes.

title: Spelling test tomorrow
scene: There's a spelling test tomorrow, and your friends are online right now.

options.text: Play online all afternoon.
Practise your words for 15 minutes, then play.

outcomes.setback: 9 out of 20. Your teacher looks disappointed.
outcomes.disaster: 3 out of 20. You redo the test at lunch while everyone else plays.
outcomes.good: 18 out of 20 and a stamp in your book.
outcomes.lucky: 20 out of 20. You're Spelling Star of the week.
outcomes.why: Fifteen minutes now beats an hour of worry later.

title: Piano or cartoons
scene: Your favourite show starts in ten minutes. You haven't done piano practice yet.

options.text: Watch the show and skip piano today.
Ten minutes of piano first, then the show.

later.seed: after five practices, a recital card unlocks

outcomes.setback: Your piano teacher can tell you didn't practise.
outcomes.disaster: You forget your piece in front of the class and have to start again.
outcomes.good: The tricky bit finally clicks.
outcomes.lucky: Your teacher gives you a harder, cooler piece to learn.
outcomes.why: Ten minutes a day beats an hour once a week.

title: Stuck on homework
scene: Your maths homework makes no sense, and it's due tomorrow.

options.text: Scribble any answers so it looks done.
Ask Mum or Dad to explain it.

outcomes.setback: Every answer comes back marked wrong.
outcomes.disaster: Your teacher keeps you in at lunch to redo it all.
outcomes.good: Once Dad explains it, it seems easy.
outcomes.lucky: You understand it so well that you help a friend the next day.
outcomes.why: Asking for help is what smart people do.

title: Hand up or head down
scene: Your teacher is explaining fractions, and you're lost. Everyone else seems to get it.

options.text: Stay quiet and hope it makes sense later.
Put your hand up and ask.

outcomes.setback: Your homework is all fractions, and you're still lost.
outcomes.disaster: You fail the fractions quiz, and the next topic builds on it.
outcomes.good: Three other kids say they were lost too. Your question helped everyone.
outcomes.lucky: Your teacher gives you a fractions game to play at home.
outcomes.why: One question now saves weeks of being confused.

title: Chapter or screen
scene: It's reading time. Your book is on the shelf, and the tablet is next to you.

options.text: Scroll videos instead.
Read half a chapter, then five minutes of videos.
Read a chapter of your book.

outcomes.setback: You can't remember a single video you watched.
outcomes.disaster: Your book is due back at the library, and you haven't read any of it. You miss the class book chat.
outcomes.good: The story gets exciting and you can't put it down.
outcomes.lucky: Your teacher picks your book review for the class newsletter.
outcomes.why: Every book makes your brain a little bigger.

title: Strange beetle
scene: You find a shiny beetle you've never seen before in the backyard.

options.text: Ignore it and go back to your game.
Look it up and start a bug journal.

later.seed: the bug journal counts toward the science fair

outcomes.setback: You never find out what it was.
outcomes.disaster: Your friend finds the same beetle and becomes the class bug expert instead of you.
outcomes.good: It's a rare jewel beetle. You draw it in your journal.
outcomes.lucky: A scientist on a nature website replies to your photo and thanks you.
outcomes.why: Curious people notice things others walk past.

title: Space or pranks
scene: There's a new documentary about the planets. Your friends are watching prank videos.

options.text: Watch prank videos with your friends.
Watch the space documentary.

outcomes.setback: You can't answer the bonus question in class about Saturn's rings.
outcomes.disaster: You copy a prank from a video and break the school tap. A note goes home.
outcomes.good: You learn that a day on Venus is longer than its year.
outcomes.lucky: Your teacher lets you present a space fact to the class.
outcomes.why: What you watch fills your head. Choose good stuff.

title: The bridge that fell
scene: Your building-set bridge collapses the moment you put a toy car on it.

options.text: Throw it in the box and give up.
Work out why it fell and build it stronger.

outcomes.setback: The box sits there unfinished for weeks.
outcomes.disaster: You give up on building sets altogether and miss the engineering club.
outcomes.good: Triangles! Your new bridge holds three cars.
outcomes.lucky: Your bridge holds a full water bottle. Dad takes a photo for the family chat.
outcomes.why: Mistakes are how engineers learn.

title: Science fair
scene: The school science fair is in three weeks. Entries need a real experiment.

options.text: Skip it this year.
Enter with an experiment.

outcomes.normal: A good project, but no prize. The judge gives you tips for next year.
outcomes.good: Highly commended. Science club cards unlock.
outcomes.lucky: First prize, and your character gets a lab coat.
outcomes.why: Everything you've learned adds up to moments like this.

title: Birthday money
scene: Grandma gave you $20 for your birthday. A new outfit for your game character costs exactly $20.

options.text: Spend it all on the outfit.
Spend $5 and bank $15.
Put it in the bank towards a new bike.

outcomes.setback: A week later the outfit is boring, and the money's gone. -30 coins.
outcomes.disaster: The school excursion needs $20 and you have nothing left. You miss out. -100 coins.
outcomes.good: Your bank balance earns its first interest.
outcomes.lucky: Grandma is so proud you saved that she adds $10 more.
outcomes.why: Money you save keeps working for you. Money you spend is gone.

title: Mystery box
scene: Your game sells mystery boxes. One might hold a super-rare skin, but most hold junk.

options.text: Buy three boxes and hope.
Save for the exact skin you actually want.

outcomes.setback: Three boxes, three pieces of junk. -30 coins.
outcomes.disaster: You keep buying "just one more" until all your savings are gone. -100 coins.
outcomes.good: You buy the skin you wanted, and it's on sale.
outcomes.lucky: The game gives away the skin free to players who saved up.
outcomes.why: Mystery boxes are built so most people lose. Choose what you're buying.

title: Three jars
scene: It's pocket money day. Dad shows you three jars: Spend, Save and Share.

options.text: Put it all in Spend and head to the shop.
Split it between the three jars.

later.seed: the Save jar grows each week

outcomes.setback: By Wednesday the money is gone, and so are the lollies. -30 coins.
outcomes.disaster: Your friend's birthday is on Saturday, and you can't afford a present. -100 coins.
outcomes.good: Your Save jar is fuller than you expected.
outcomes.lucky: Your Share jar buys a toy for the school charity drive, and you get a thank-you card.
outcomes.why: A plan for your money means you're never caught short.

title: Let it grow
scene: You have 300 coins. The bank pays interest every Sunday if you leave them there.

options.text: Spend them on decorations for your room now.
Leave them in the bank for a month.

outcomes.setback: The decorations look great, but nothing grows. -30 coins.
outcomes.disaster: You spend it all, and then the bike you wanted goes on sale. You can't buy it. -100 coins.
outcomes.good: After four Sundays, your 300 coins are 324.
outcomes.lucky: The bank runs a bonus month, and your interest doubles.
outcomes.why: Interest is money that money earns while you sleep.

title: Lemonade stand
scene: It's going to be hot on Saturday. You could sell lemonade outside the house.

options.text: Sleep in and play games all morning.
Make lemonade and a sign, and set up the stand.

outcomes.setback: The kid next door sets up a stand instead and makes the money. -30 coins.
outcomes.disaster: You're bored all weekend and spend your pocket money on drinks at the shop. -100 coins.
outcomes.good: You sell out by lunchtime.
outcomes.lucky: A neighbour orders lemonade for her whole party.
outcomes.why: Earning money takes effort, and it feels great.

title: Same toy, cheaper
scene: The toy you want is $40 here. Mum says the same toy is $25 at another shop across town.

options.text: Buy it here, right now.
Wait until Saturday and buy it at the cheaper shop.

outcomes.setback: You find the same toy cheaper the next day. -30 coins.
outcomes.disaster: You spent so much that there's nothing left for the movies with your friends. -100 coins.
outcomes.good: You save $15 and buy a book with the change.
outcomes.lucky: The cheaper shop has a sale. You get it for $20.
outcomes.why: Checking prices first means more money for other things.

title: Halfway to the bike
scene: You're halfway to saving for a new bike. A cool toy is on sale at the shops.

options.text: Buy the toy. The bike can wait.
Walk past the toy and keep saving.

outcomes.setback: The toy breaks in a week. -30 coins.
outcomes.disaster: Summer comes, your friends are riding new bikes, and you're back to the start. -100 coins.
outcomes.good: You reach three-quarters of your goal.
outcomes.lucky: The bike shop has a sale. You can buy it this weekend.
outcomes.why: Small wants can steal your big goals.

title: Wash the car
scene: Dad offers 50 coins if you wash the car this afternoon. Your game is calling.

options.text: Say no and keep playing.
Wash the car properly, wheels and all.

outcomes.setback: Your friend down the street washes your dad's car instead. -30 coins.
outcomes.disaster: You need money for the school disco and there's none left. You miss it. -100 coins.
outcomes.good: Dad is so pleased he asks you to do it every month.
outcomes.lucky: The neighbours see your work and ask you to wash their car too.
outcomes.why: Hard work today is money in your pocket tomorrow.

title: Mum's card
scene: A game on Mum's tablet says "Buy 500 gems now!" Mum's card is saved, and she's in the shower.

options.text: Tap Buy. She'll never notice.
Close the game and ask Mum later.

outcomes.setback: Mum gets an email receipt within a minute. No game time for a week. -30 coins.
outcomes.disaster: You buy gems five times before Mum's bank calls her. You must pay it back from your savings. Mum and Dad are very disappointed. -200 coins.
outcomes.good: Mum says yes to a small gem pack, because you asked.
outcomes.lucky: Mum is so impressed you asked that she shows you how to earn gems free in the game.
outcomes.why: Money that isn't yours is never yours to spend.

title: Quiz answers
scene: Your friend shows you the answers to tomorrow's quiz. He got them from the teacher's desk.

options.text: Copy them.
Say no thanks and study yourself.

outcomes.setback: You get full marks but feel bad all day.
outcomes.disaster: The teacher spots identical answers. Zero marks, a note home, and Mum and Dad find out.
outcomes.good: You get 16 out of 20, all by yourself.
outcomes.lucky: The teacher changes the quiz at the last minute. You're ready and your friend isn't.
outcomes.why: Your marks should be yours. Cheating steals from you most.

title: Chocolate dare
scene: Your mates dare you to take a chocolate from the corner shop without paying.

options.text: Take it. Everyone will laugh.
Say no and walk out.

outcomes.setback: The shopkeeper gives you a long, suspicious look every time you go in.
outcomes.disaster: You're caught. The shopkeeper bans you and calls home, and Mum and Dad come to collect you.
outcomes.good: One mate walks out with you. He didn't want to do it either.
outcomes.lucky: The shopkeeper saw you say no and gives you a free icy pole.
outcomes.why: Real friends don't dare you to do wrong.

title: The broken mug
scene: You were throwing a ball inside and broke Mum's favourite mug. The dog is right there.

options.text: Say the dog knocked it over.
Tell Mum the truth and say sorry.

outcomes.setback: The dog gets sent outside, and you feel terrible.
outcomes.disaster: Mum finds the ball under the couch. Now it's about the lie, not the mug. No screens for a week.
outcomes.good: Mum is sad about the mug, but proud you told her.
outcomes.lucky: You use your own coins to buy Mum a new mug, and she uses it every day.
outcomes.why: Owning up is hard for a minute. Lying is hard for much longer.

title: Dog's dinner
scene: It's the dog's dinner time, but you're one level from beating your game.

options.text: Finish the level. The dog can wait.
Pause and feed the dog now.

outcomes.setback: The dog whines at the door until you're finally done.
outcomes.disaster: You forget completely. The dog gets into the bin and makes a huge mess you have to clean up.
outcomes.good: The dog licks your face, and you beat the level straight after.
outcomes.lucky: Dad sees you pause your game and gives you an extra half-hour on the weekend.
outcomes.why: Someone depends on you. That matters more than a game.

title: The new kid
scene: A new kid is sitting alone at lunch. Your friends are waving you over.

options.text: Go sit with your friends.
Invite the new kid to sit with your group.

outcomes.setback: The new kid sits alone all week.
outcomes.disaster: Later you find out the new kid felt so lonely they asked to change schools.
outcomes.good: The new kid knows heaps about space, just like you.
outcomes.lucky: The new kid becomes one of your best friends.
outcomes.why: Being kind costs nothing and can change someone's whole year.

title: Dinner's ready
scene: Dad calls out to set the table. You're right in the middle of a video.

options.text: Pretend you didn't hear.
Pause it and set the table.

outcomes.setback: Dad sets it himself and looks tired.
outcomes.disaster: Dad turns off the tablet. No more videos tonight.
outcomes.good: Dinner is your favourite, and you get first pick.
outcomes.lucky: Dad says, "Thanks, mate. You choose Friday's movie."
outcomes.why: A family works when everyone pitches in.

title: Ten dollars
scene: You find $10 on the playground. Nobody saw you pick it up.

options.text: Keep it. Finders keepers.
Hand it in at the office.

outcomes.setback: You hear a little kid crying because she lost her canteen money.
outcomes.disaster: Someone did see you. Your teacher asks about it in front of the class.
outcomes.good: The little kid gets her money back and her mum thanks you.
outcomes.lucky: You get a Values Award at assembly.
outcomes.why: Honesty is what you do when nobody is watching.

title: School captain
scene: Nominations are open for school captain. Teachers pick students who are kind, honest and reliable.

options.text: Don't nominate this year.
Nominate and give a speech.

outcomes.normal: You're not picked, but your speech gets a big clap.
outcomes.good: You're made house captain. Leader cards unlock.
outcomes.lucky: You're school captain, and your character gets a captain's badge.
outcomes.why: People trust you with big jobs when you've done the small ones well.

title: Laughing along
scene: Your friends are teasing a younger kid about his glasses. They look at you to join in.

options.text: Laugh along so they don't tease you.
Tell them to stop and walk over to the kid.

outcomes.setback: The younger kid looks at you like you're one of them.
outcomes.disaster: A teacher sees the whole group. Everyone, including you, gets a note home.
outcomes.good: Your friends stop. One says sorry.
outcomes.lucky: The kid's big sister thanks you, and she's the captain of the soccer team.
outcomes.why: Standing up for someone takes courage. That's what real strength is.
